explanation: Restaurant bills in France legally include a service charge (service compris), so waitstaff are already paid for service and tipping is not expected or required. Rounding up the bill or leaving a few euros in cash for good service is a nice, purely optional gesture, not an obligation calculated as a percentage.
local_tip: Pay the bill as printed, and if service was good, just round up to the nearest euro or leave a couple of coins in cash.

also_check.note: Tipping is unnecessary and can even confuse or embarrass staff; excellent service is the cultural default, not something paid extra for.
Tipping 15-20% at restaurants is the customary, near-mandatory norm since many service workers rely on tips for income.
A 'coperto' (cover charge) is often added to the bill and is separate from tipping; tipping itself is optional, with a few euros appreciated but not expected.
